title: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator
summary: The AWS Certified SysOps Administrator - Associate exam, code SOA-C02, is aimed at engineers who already run workloads on Amazon Web Services and now want to prove they can operate them day to day. It sits at associate level, one step above the cloud practitioner entry point and alongside the solutions architect and developer associate exams, but its focus is operations rather than design or code. Passing it tells an employer that you can deploy, monitor, secure, back up and troubleshoot real accounts, and that you understand cost and reliability trade-offs. The exam is proctored and mixes multiple choice and multiple response questions with hands-on lab items performed in a live AWS console environment. It leads to roles such as cloud operations engineer, site reliability engineer, systems administrator and cloud support engineer. This is an independent study guide and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Amazon Web Services.

beginner.definition: This is a professional certificate from Amazon Web Services, often shortened to AWS, that proves you can run systems in their cloud. It is an associate level exam, which means it expects some real hands-on time with the platform. The exam code is SOA-C02 and the full name is AWS Certified SysOps Administrator. SysOps simply means system operations, the work of keeping services healthy after they are built.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many companies now rent their computers from a cloud provider instead of owning servers. They need people who can keep those rented systems fast, safe and cheap. This certificate proves you have done that work, not just read about it. It helps you move from a help desk or junior administrator job into a cloud operations role. Employers also use it as evidence that you understand monitoring, backups and access control in a real account.
howItWorks: Start by getting comfortable with the AWS console and the command line interface, because you must actually build and fix things rather than only answer theory questions.
Study each exam domain in turn, and for every topic create the resource yourself in a free test account and then delete it again.
Practise reading logs and metrics so you can explain why a service is slow, failing or more expensive than expected.
Learn the shared responsibility model, meaning which security tasks belong to AWS and which belong to you.
Take practice tests to find weak areas, then go back to the console and rebuild those parts by hand.
On exam day you answer multiple choice questions and also complete lab tasks inside a live AWS environment.
beginner.example: Imagine you rent a flat instead of buying a house. The landlord keeps the building standing, but you still decide who gets a key, what furniture fits and when to call a repair service. Cloud computing works the same way. AWS keeps the data centres running, and you decide who can log in, how much space you use and what happens when a hard disk fails. A SysOps administrator is the person who holds the keys, watches the electricity bill and knows which fuse to reset at two in the morning.
takeaways: You need hands-on time in a real AWS account, because the lab questions test practical actions, not just memory.
Operations work is about monitoring, security, reliability and cost, so study all four together rather than separately.
Always check the current exam guide on the AWS website, because services and domain weights change over time.

objectives: Explain how the AWS shared responsibility model divides security duties between the provider and the customer
Deploy and configure compute, storage and network resources using the console, the command line and templates
Collect and interpret metrics, logs and traces in order to detect and diagnose unhealthy workloads
Implement identity, access and network controls that follow least privilege and business requirements
Design backup, recovery and high availability arrangements that meet stated recovery targets
Identify and reduce unnecessary cloud spending while keeping performance acceptable

chapters.title: Monitoring, logging and remediation
objectives: Create alarms and dashboards that surface unhealthy resources before users notice
Interpret CloudWatch metrics, logs and log insights queries to locate the cause of an incident
Automate a corrective response such as restarting, resizing or replacing a failing resource
Configure event driven actions that react to changes in account configuration or service state
Distinguish between symptoms users report and the underlying resource metric that explains them

chapters.title: Reliability and business continuity
objectives: Choose storage and database options that match the required durability and availability level
Design multi availability zone and multi region arrangements and explain the trade-offs of each
Implement backup schedules, retention rules and restore procedures, then test that a restore works
Describe recovery time objective and recovery point objective and select a strategy that meets them
Scale resources automatically in response to demand without causing instability

chapters.title: Deployment, provisioning and automation
objectives: Provision repeatable environments from templates instead of building resources by hand
Run and troubleshoot deployment pipelines that release application changes safely
Use managed container and serverless services and explain when each one is appropriate
Apply tagging and naming standards that make resources traceable and reportable
Roll back or repair a failed deployment without taking the whole service offline

chapters.title: Security and compliance
objectives: Write identity and access policies that grant only the permissions a task genuinely requires
Configure encryption for data at rest and in transit and manage the keys that protect it
Control network reachability with security groups, network access control lists and private endpoints
Detect and respond to suspicious activity by using logging, findings and alerting services
Store secrets and credentials so that they are never written into source code or plain text files

chapters.title: Networking and content delivery
objectives: Design virtual private cloud, subnet and route table layouts that separate public and private tiers
Connect on premises networks or other cloud networks to a virtual private cloud securely
Resolve name resolution and connectivity faults across accounts, regions and network boundaries
Use a content delivery network and caching layers to reduce latency and origin load
Balance traffic across targets and health check them so that unhealthy targets stop receiving requests

chapters.title: Cost and performance optimisation
objectives: Analyse billing and usage reports to find where money is being wasted
Right size compute, storage and database resources against measured demand
Select pricing models such as reserved or spot capacity and explain when each one saves money
Apply storage lifecycle rules that move or delete data as it ages
Improve an application response time by finding and removing the real bottleneck
